subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: Should this issue stay open as the focused current-PID restart/recovery lock tracker, or should maintainers close it after moving the remaining live current-PID lock work to a broader canonical issue?
rationale: The original boot cleanup is partly implemented and shipped, but deciding when a live gateway-owned lock may be reclaimed crosses a session data-integrity boundary that source inspection should not settle automatically.

options.title: Keep Focused Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open for same-PID restart/recovery lock semantics while related PRs handle narrower compaction and delivery fixes.

options.title: Move To Broader Lock Tracker
options.body: Close only after explicitly linking the remaining live current-PID lock behavior to a canonical issue such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/86538 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/100425.

options.title: Declare Boot-Sweep Complete
options.body: Treat the original boot-sweep request as complete and open a narrower follow-up for runtime/recovery live current-PID lock leaks.

recommendation.title: Keep Focused Tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for same-PID restart/recovery lock semantics while related PRs handle narrower compaction and delivery fixes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on session write-lock hardening and is closest to the live-lock policy boundary.
